title: Key irregulars: aller, faire, vouloir, pouvoir
goal: By the end of this lesson you can conjugate aller, faire, vouloir and pouvoir in the present, use them with an infinitive (je veux manger, je peux venir), and understand the Quebec 'j'vas' you hear everywhere.

body: *aller* ends in -er but is completely irregular. Use it for movement (*Je vais à Montréal*) and for how someone is doing (*Comment allez-vous? Je vais bien*).
*à* + *le* contracts to *au*, and *à* + *les* to *aux*: *Je vais au café, aux toilettes*. *À la* and *à l'* don't change.
learn.tip: à + le = au; à + les = aux. Je vais au dépanneur.

body: *faire* covers 'do' and 'make': *Je fais un gâteau* (I'm making a cake), *Qu'est-ce que tu fais?* (What are you doing?). It's also used for the weather (*Il fait beau, il fait froid*) and many activities (*faire du sport, faire l'épicerie*).
Note the irregular *vous faites* (never 'faisez') and *ils font*.

learn.h: Vouloir and pouvoir: want and can
body: *vouloir* (to want) and *pouvoir* (can, to be able to) follow the same pattern: *-x, -x, -t* in the singular, then a vowel change in *ils veulent / ils peuvent*.
Both are often followed directly by an infinitive: *Je veux manger. Tu peux venir?* To order politely, use *je voudrais* (I would like) instead of *je veux*, which can sound blunt.
learn.tip: At a counter: Je voudrais un café, s'il vous plaît.

body: With all four verbs, a second verb stays in the infinitive: *Je vais manger* (I'm going to eat), *On peut parler?* (Can we talk?), *Tu veux jouer?* (Do you want to play?).
*aller* + infinitive is the near future, which you will study in detail later: *Je vais travailler demain.*
In Quebec speech, *je vais* is very often *j'vas* (from an old form *je vas*): *J'vas au dépanneur.* It is informal but heard everywhere, from all ages.

You'll also hear *m'as* for *je vais* + infinitive: *M'as y aller* (I'm gonna go). And *être capable* often replaces *pouvoir*: *Chu pas capable* = I can't. Recognise these; use the standard forms in writing.

examples.en: I'm going to the convenience store.
I do the groceries on Saturdays.
examples.note: faire l'épicerie: very Quebec, standard French too

examples.fr: Je voudrais un café, s'il vous plaît.

examples.en: Do you want to play outside?
I'm going to the movies tonight.

quebec.intro: In Quebec speech, je vais is very often j'vas. You'll also hear m'as (I'm gonna) and chu capable / chu pas capable for 'I can / I can't'.

items.en: I'm going to the convenience store.

items.note: faire l'épicerie is the normal Quebec expression

drills.q: The most polite way to order is…
options: Je voudrais un café, s'il vous plaît.

drills.en: Do you want to play outside?

a: Je voudrais un café, s'il vous plaît.
Je voudrais un café, s'il te plaît.
drills.why: je voudrais is the polite form.

vocab.ex: Qu'est-ce que tu fais ce soir?

pron.tip: noo fuh-ZÕ: the ai sounds like 'uh'.
Open vowel: eel VULL, eel PUV.
Quebec casual: zhvaw, with a long deep a.

dialogue.en: I'm going to do the groceries in the morning.

dialogue.fr: Et l'après-midi? Tu veux aller au cinéma?
dialogue.en: And in the afternoon? Do you want to go to the movies?

dialogue.fr: Oui, mais je peux seulement après trois heures.
dialogue.en: Yes, but I can only go after three.

dialogue.fr: Pas de problème. On va au cinéma à quatre heures.
dialogue.en: No problem. We'll go to the movies at four.

questions.q: What is B doing Saturday morning?
What time will they go to the movies?

speak.prompt: Say where you are going this weekend and what you are going to do.
speak.model: Samedi, je vais au marché. Je vais faire l'épicerie. Dimanche, je vais au cinéma.

speak.prompt: Order two things politely at a café.
speak.model: Bonjour! Je voudrais un café et un muffin, s'il vous plaît.

speak.prompt: Ask a friend if they want to come and if they can come tomorrow.
speak.model: Tu veux venir? Tu peux venir demain?

write.prompt: Write 5–6 sentences about your plans for Saturday using aller, faire, vouloir and pouvoir.
write.model: Samedi, je vais faire l'épicerie. Après, je vais au parc avec mes enfants. Ils veulent jouer dehors. Le soir, on peut aller au cinéma. Je voudrais voir un film québécois.

quiz.q: The ils form of vouloir is…
After vouloir and pouvoir, the next verb is…
quiz.why: Je veux manger, je peux venir.

quiz.q: 'M'as y aller' is casual Quebec for…

options: I'm not capable of being good
quiz.why: être capable often replaces pouvoir in Quebec.
